name: Southern Copper Corporation

profile.description: Southern Copper Corporation is an integrated copper mining, smelting, and refining company operating in Peru, Mexico, Argentina, and Chile. It produces copper, molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold from open-pit and underground mines. The company holds 164,805 hectares in Peru and 505,788 hectares in Mexico. A subsidiary of Americas Mining Corporation (Grupo Mexico).

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): SCCO delivered record FY2025 revenue of $13.4B (up 17% YoY) and followed with a record Q1 2026 — $4.25B revenue (up 36% QoQ), $1.92 EPS (up 67%), and $1.58B net income [1][4]. The Tia Maria project in Peru targets 2027 commissioning, adding 120,000 tonnes/year copper capacity. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered products or quantified AI-driven operational savings in mining operations. Market Share (2/2): SCCO is the world's fifth-largest integrated copper producer by output and the largest copper producer in Mexico, with dominant positions across copper, molybdenum, and zinc in Latin America; the company holds the world's largest copper reserves [1][2]. Pipeline (2/2): Over $15B in capital investments outlined, raised 2026 production guidance for copper, molybdenum, and silver, and Buenavista zinc concentrator at full capacity expected to lift zinc output 31% [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Mining-level exploration investment across 98,634 hectares in Argentina and 28,453 in Chile, but R&D spend is below industry average as a percentage of revenue.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Southern Copper articulates responsibility to communities and sustainable mining for global infrastructure needs, but the mission reads as standard industry language without distinctive purpose beyond operational excellence [2]. Community Impact (2/2): The company has allocated approximately $379.9M since 2019 to social and philanthropic projects supporting UN Sustainable Development Goals in communities near operations in Peru and Mexico, a significant and specific commitment [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): SCCO maintains 16,617 employees across multiple countries with a stable workforce; the organization transitioned smoothly after CEO Oscar Gonzalez Rocha's sudden death in April 2026, with Leonardo Contreras Lerdo de Tejada appointed as successor, demonstrating institutional resilience [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Americas Mining Corporation holds a controlling ~88% stake; no evidence of meaningful net insider buying by independent executives.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Southern Copper's financial profile is exceptional. D/E of 67% sits below the 70% target, ROE of 46.5% far exceeds the 15% threshold, and profit margin of 32.3% reflects outstanding operational efficiency [1][5]. Revenue growth of 17% YoY for FY2025 and 10.9% 5-year CAGR demonstrate sustained cyclical momentum. Forward P/E of 25.2x is elevated for a commodity producer, reflecting the copper supercycle premium. The 31-year consecutive dividend history and 8.2% 5-year CAGR anchor the income profile, though the variable policy tied to copper prices limits consecutive growth years to 2 and the 60.5% payout ratio exceeds the 40% ideal [5]. Liquidity floor easily cleared: 1.05M avg volume x $181.54 = $190.6M daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Copper mining is a physical-world operation that AI structurally cannot displace — extracting, smelting, and refining metals from underground and open-pit mines requires heavy equipment, geological expertise, and physical infrastructure immune to software substitution [2]. The global copper deficit projected through 2026+ directly benefits SCCO as AI data center buildout accelerates demand for copper wiring, power infrastructure, and semiconductor interconnects [1]. AI Opportunity (1/1): While SCCO does not sell AI products, it is a direct infrastructure beneficiary — copper is an essential input for AI data centers, EV charging networks, and semiconductor manufacturing, all scaling rapidly; management cited growing data center copper demand in Q1 2026 earnings commentary [4].

infinite_game.summary: Southern Copper plays a moderately infinite game, anchored by a 70+ year operating history, $15B+ long-term capital investment program, and institutional resilience demonstrated when the organization continued seamlessly after the CEO's sudden death in April 2026 [2]. The variable dividend policy tied to copper prices rather than quarterly smoothing shows cyclical awareness. However, the company operates under a controlling parent (Grupo Mexico), which limits strategic independence, and the Just Cause is industry-standard rather than transformative.

just_cause.analysis: Southern Copper's purpose of supplying essential copper for global infrastructure is important but not distinctive — any copper miner could make the same claim. The company articulates commitment to sustainability and community development, backed by $379.9M in social investment since 2019, but the Just Cause is more industry-standard than transformative [3]. Score: 1/3 points.

trusting_teams.analysis: The company maintains 16,617 employees across Peru, Mexico, and the US. The organization demonstrated institutional resilience when CEO Oscar Gonzalez Rocha died suddenly in April 2026 — Leonardo Contreras Lerdo de Tejada was appointed as successor and Q1 2026 delivered record results, suggesting the institution transcends any single leader [2][4]. Glassdoor ratings of 4/5 with 77% recommending the company indicate adequate employee satisfaction. Score: 1/2 points.

worthy_rivals.analysis: SCCO positions itself as the lowest-cost integrated copper producer rather than framing competition as a war against Freeport-McMoRan, BHP, or Codelco. Management's focus on operational efficiency, reserve development, and cost discipline reflects an improvement-oriented rather than victory-oriented competitive mindset [1]. Score: 1/1 point.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Southern Copper has diversified from pure copper into molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold production, and expanded geographically from Peru to Mexico, Argentina, and Chile. The Buenavista zinc concentrator expansion (31% output increase) shows continued evolution [4]. However, the core business model — mine, smelt, refine — has remained fundamentally unchanged for decades. Score: 1/2 points.

courage_to_lead.analysis: SCCO has demonstrated courage by persevering with the Tia Maria project in Peru despite years of community opposition and permitting delays, committing $15B+ in capital investments through commodity cycles, and maintaining a variable dividend policy that prioritizes reinvestment over payout smoothing [1][3]. Investing through the 2019-2020 copper downturn when peers cut capex showed long-term conviction. Score: 1/2 points.

investment_thesis: Southern Copper is a premier copper play benefiting from the structural copper supercycle driven by AI data center buildout, EV adoption, and grid electrification. Q1 2026 delivered record results — $4.25B revenue (up 36%), $1.92 EPS (up 67%), and $1.58B net income — demonstrating accelerating momentum [4]. FY2025 revenue reached $13.4B with 32.3% profit margins, 46.5% ROE, and D/E of just 67% [1][5]. The 31-year dividend history with 8.2% 5-year CAGR provides income alongside growth exposure. The $15B+ capital investment program and Tia Maria commissioning (2027) position SCCO for sustained production growth as the global copper deficit widens.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on commodity cyclicality and valuation. Forward P/E of 25.2x is expensive for a mining company, pricing in a perfect copper supercycle scenario. CEO Oscar Gonzalez Rocha's death in April 2026 after a 26-year tenure created a generational leadership transition, though the appointment of Leonardo Contreras Lerdo de Tejada has stabilized governance [2]. SCCO is controlled by Americas Mining Corporation (Grupo Mexico) with ~88% ownership, raising minority shareholder governance concerns. Peru and Mexico face political instability — mining nationalism, permitting delays, and community opposition have historically disrupted operations. The variable dividend policy means income is unreliable in copper downturns — annual dividends ranged from $0.17 (2016) to $3.82+ in recent years, and consecutive growth years stand at only 2 [5]. A 30-40% copper price correction would severely compress margins.
key_catalysts: Tia Maria copper project in Peru targeting 2027 commissioning, adding 120,000 tonnes/year of capacity to SCCO's production base, with $15B+ total capital investment pipeline [1][4]
AI data center and EV infrastructure buildout driving projected global copper deficit through 2026+, supporting elevated copper prices and SCCO's record Q1 2026 margins [4]
Buenavista zinc concentrator at full capacity expected to lift zinc output 31%, diversifying revenue streams beyond copper [4]
key_risks: Commodity price cyclicality — copper prices can decline 30-40% in recessions, compressing margins and triggering dividend cuts, as seen in 2015-2016 when annual dividends fell to $0.17 per share [5]

Latin American political and permitting risk — Peru and Mexico face mining nationalism, community opposition, and regulatory uncertainty that could delay or cancel the Tia Maria and other expansion projects [3]
Controlling shareholder governance — Grupo Mexico's ~88% ownership limits minority shareholder influence on capital allocation, dividend policy, and related-party transactions [2]
